shared_contract.note: This file proposes business payloads, not a replacement for the shared scenario, result, trace, or staging contracts. Parent approval of all 15 researched scenarios remains a separate gate.

data_excluded: Real people, patients, PHI, provider identifiers, trial records, customer data, credentials, and client systems
Patient demographics, clinical observations, test results, diagnoses, treatments, consent forms, and enrollment lists
Actual product labeling or actual specimen suitability rules represented as invented mock policy
boundaries.permitted_outcome: Read mock exported tables, reconcile their administrative evidence, and produce a deterministic review-ready packet with unresolved issues and provenance.
prohibited_outcomes: Clinical decisions, trial enrollment or site activation approval
Specimen acceptance or rejection for patient care, clinical ordering, diagnosis, or treatment
Product use, release, disposal, physical quarantine, or inventory movement authorization
Regulatory compliance, validated-system, or independent human-review claims
Live business writes, notifications, scheduling, connections, publication, or native UI actions
boundaries.human_boundary: Qualified trial, laboratory, and quality reviewers retain all actual interpretation and disposition. A packet marked completed has completed file processing only; rejected refers only to an invalid input packet, never a specimen or product.

connections.note: Synthetic tables model exported files. No endpoint, authentication, CTMS, LIS, EHR, sensor, inventory, manufacturer, or public-health integration is provisioned or verified.

native.prerequisites: Approved Computer Use tools restored, an unlocked accessible session, and parent-coordinated authorization.
native.no_workaround: No alternate browser, Playwright, private API, cookie, token, shell, or model/skill route.
native.output_rule: Only actual native-generated plugins may enter root output. No locally generated ZIP or placeholder is native evidence.

sources.title: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice, final version adopted 06 January 2025
sources.scope: Annex 1, Appendix C: management and essentiality of trial records; a non-participant administrative subset only.
supported_claims: C.2.1 addresses identifiable, appropriately version-controlled records with relevant author, reviewer, approver, date, and signature information.
C.2.3-C.2.6 address repositories, record locations, version history, timely filing, completeness, readability, access, and traceable alterations.
C.3.1-C.3.3 make essentiality contextual; the essential-records table is not exhaustive and some records depend on trial design and conduct.
The table includes signed protocols and amendments, dated IRB/IEC opinions, qualifications, trial-specific training, and delegation documentation.
sources.limitations: This guideline is not a universal checklist, annual-expiry mandate, or automatic readiness decision. The synthetic checklist, expiry calculations, warning windows, and document-ranking rules are local sample policies. No participant records are included.

retrieval.method: Public HTTPS download; text extracted with already-installed pdftotext; PDF page references checked with already-installed pypdf.
locators: Appendix C.2, printed pages 63-64, PDF pages 70-71
Appendix C.3 and essential-records table, printed pages 64-68, PDF pages 71-75
retrieval.short_quote: Records should be identifiable and version controlled

sources.title: E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice (GCP)
sources.scope: FDA final-guidance announcement and its risk-proportionate framing.
supported_claims: FDA announces final E6(R3) guidance and describes flexible, risk-based approaches.
The announcement describes clarified sponsor and investigator responsibilities and proportionality throughout the trial lifecycle.
sources.limitations: The HTML page supports the announcement and framing only. Detailed essential-record claims cite the independently retrieved ICH PDF, not this landing page or its unretrieved FDA download.

retrieval.edition_observed: Final guidance announcement; no publication date inferred from the fetched body.

sources.title: Temperature Monitoring
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.scope: Immunization-product temperature monitoring, excursion documentation, and escalation.
supported_claims: An excursion is evaluated against the relevant manufacturer's package insert or EUA fact sheet, not a universal temperature band.
Event documentation includes timing, temperatures, potentially affected inventory and lots, actions, contacts, and instructions received.
CDC describes labeling and separating exposed inventory, retaining it rather than automatically discarding it, and obtaining manufacturer or immunization-program guidance.
Magnitude and time outside the recommended range are information manufacturers use when assessing an excursion.
sources.limitations: The scenario only prepares an evidence packet. It cannot label or move physical stock, contact authorities, determine viability, repeat a dose, or authorize use/disposal. Temperature profiles and sample-hold duration estimation are invented fixture policies, not CDC or product instructions.

retrieval.edition_observed: Live page retrieved 2026-09-14; no page revision date inferred.
locators: Perform the following steps in the event of a temperature excursion

sources.title: Vaccine Storage and Handling
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.scope: Toolkit scope, July 2026 updates, product-specific information, and limitations of compliance language.
supported_claims: The toolkit applies to vaccines and RSV monoclonal antibody products.
The page reports a full-toolkit update on 2026-07-14, including storage of products with different temperature ranges.
Product-specific guidance and jurisdiction-specific program requirements must be distinguished.
CDC cautions that vendor compliance language does not establish CDC validation or endorsement.
sources.limitations: Vaccine guidance is not generalized to every medical supply. No real licensed product or manufacturer profile is modeled; no CDC, VFC, or regulatory compliance is asserted.

retrieval.edition_observed: Page explicitly states full toolkit updated 2026-07-14.
locators: Where to Find Current, Product-specific Storage and Handling Guidance

sources.title: State Operations Manual, Appendix C - Survey Procedures and Interpretive Guidelines for Laboratories and Laboratory Services
sources.scope: Relevant CLIA nonwaived-test quality-system provisions and interpretive guidance, not a complete regulatory analysis.
supported_claims: D5203 / 42 CFR 493.1232 addresses positive identification through receipt, accessioning, and subsequent laboratory phases.
D5301 and D5305 / 493.1241(a),(c) address authorized requests and requisition information, including identifiers, requested tests, specimen source, and collection date/time as applicable.
D5309 / 493.1241(e) addresses accurate transcription of requisition information into a record system or LIS.
D5311 / 493.1242(a) addresses written specimen-handling procedures, including labeling and processing; its acceptability/rejection provisions remain outside this scenario.
D5313 / 493.1242(b) requires documenting the date and time of specimen receipt.
D5391 / 493.1249(a) addresses ongoing monitoring, assessment, and correction of preanalytic-system problems.
sources.limitations: The mock intentionally omits clinical demographics, actual authorized-person verification, suitability/rejection criteria, testing, results, and many CLIA requirements. Its synthetic subject tokens are not real patient identifiers. An administrative accession SLA is not a CLIA time limit, and this report is not CLIA compliance.

retrieval.method: Public HTTPS download; text extracted with already-installed pdftotext; PDF page references checked with already-installed pypdf.
retrieval.edition_observed: Cover: Rev. 236, issued 2026-01-23. The cited D5203/D5301-D5313/D5391 sections show Rev. 233, issued/effective/implementation 2025-09-12.
retrieval.short_quote: The laboratory must document the date and time it receives a specimen.

sources.title: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)
sources.scope: CLIA program scope and test-complexity context.
supported_claims: CMS describes CLIA as regulating human laboratory testing for health assessment or diagnosis, prevention, or treatment.
The page distinguishes requirements according to test-method complexity.
sources.limitations: This overview is used to bound claims, not to establish a particular accession algorithm, certification outcome, or universal rule for every laboratory.

retrieval.edition_observed: Live page retrieved 2026-09-14; no page revision date inferred.

sources.title: Laboratory quality management system: handbook
sources.scope: Laboratory quality management includes management, administration, and laboratory work.
supported_claims: The publication overview explicitly includes administrative stakeholders in health laboratory quality management.
sources.limitations: Only the public overview was fetched. No handbook chapter, ISO text, specimen rule, or accreditation claim is inferred from it.

retrieval.edition_observed: Publication overview; publication date not inferred from the fetched body.

discovery_exclusions: Search summaries are discovery aids only. Incorrect ICH section labels and an invented older PDF URL were replaced by the fetched final guideline and its actual Appendix C.
The attempted FDA media/169090 download returned Not found. Its contents were not treated as retrieved evidence; the FDA HTML announcement and independently fetched ICH PDF are distinguished.
eCFR returned an automated-access/CAPTCHA notice, not regulatory text. No bypass was attempted and that response supports no substantive claim.
Guessed govinfo annual-section URLs returned error pages and an obsolete CMS PDF path returned 404; none is a source in this catalog.
Unverified search-summary laboratory section titles and third-party citations were discarded in favor of the actual CMS manual's D-tags and text.
No whole source document or full extraction is committed. The catalog retains links, limited quotations, locators, retrieval facts, and hashes where actually obtained.

result_envelope.outputs: Scenario-specific object; no business fields outside outputs.
result_envelope.exceptions: Ordered objects containing code and message, with optional entity IDs, rule IDs, and source references.

proposed_limits.behavior: Validate positive bounded limits before joins. Reject an over-limit payload explicitly; never truncate a decision set or retry until success.

validation_rules: Reject malformed required types, unsupported fields, invalid date/timestamp syntax, non-finite values, booleans masquerading as integers, and invalid policy configuration before business evaluation.
Date-only values are Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD; timestamps are whole-second UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. No local clock, implicit timezone, float duration, or wall-clock output.

Exact repeated rows with the same record ID collapse deterministically with a duplicate count and a duplicate-evidence exception. Conflicting values for the same key quarantine that entity and its dependent evaluations; never first-wins.

Future evidence is excluded from the as-of assessment and listed with its reason. Known missing, contradictory, unavailable, and out-of-scope evidence remains explicit rather than becoming a successful default.
Use exact synthetic keys only. No name-based or fuzzy identity joins, external enrichment, generated clinical facts, or free-text instructions executed as code.

Sort result arrays by documented business keys and reason priority. Preserve source table and record IDs, selected/excluded record IDs, policy IDs, and duplicate multiplicities; input hashes belong to the shared trace.

A completed packet can include unresolved review tasks. Any warning, duplicate, or review issue makes the status completed_with_exceptions; a syntactically/business-structurally unusable payload is rejected.
independent_golden_strategy: After catalog approval, freeze procedure rules and write all five expected JSON envelopes before the first baseline execution.
Derive expectation tables from explicit requirement grids, interval intersections, or join truth tables, with manual date arithmetic and per-case count-conservation assertions.
Document sector-author reasoning, not a claim of independent human review. A separate arithmetic check may use stdlib date/integer operations without importing the baseline.
Never execute baseline code to author expected values, copy baseline outputs, import expected files in the solver, or change a golden merely to silence a mismatch.
On a mismatch, reconcile the written rule, input fact, and independently derived assertion; correct the faulty side with an explicit reason.
Withheld holdouts, negative cases, derivations, expected files, this research catalog, baseline code, and baseline outputs are never Creator inputs.
common_design.future_execution_interface: baseline.py implements solve(payload) -> (result, events), uses Python stdlib plus scenario_support.run_cli, and simulates exported-data processing only.

future_trace_video.events: Actual computed stage snapshots, at least six meaningful demo events spanning input, validation, join, decision, exception, and output. First input, last output; bounded tables and facts follow SCENARIO_CONTRACT.md.
future_trace_video.label: Synthetic baseline execution visualization - not Cowork or a live system
future_trace_video.visual_only_policy: Internal storyboard hints below are presentation observations, not concealed clinical or safety rules. Do not copy them into a native authoring prompt; any visual-observation evaluation is distinct from deterministic business comparisons.

native_capabilities.needed_for: Allowed procedure, workflow, connections, demo payload, and media inputs
Review packet and actual generated output plugin
Independent authoring, bounded joins, dates, integer arithmetic, and reports
Actual observation of the baseline demonstration

native_gaps: Current access gate prevents observing any required native capability or running the Creator.
File exports do not establish CTMS/LIS/EHR access, authenticated records, sensor fidelity, signatures, or permissions.
Native attachment/media observation and independent plugin execution must be evidenced separately; historical native work is not inherited.

If a required native capability is missing, report a gap. No backend, custom MCP authoring service, external model/media API, OCR/transcription service, runner, device agent, scheduler, resource provisioning, or installer is allowed.

scenarios.title: Clinical-trial site essential-document completeness and expiry review packet
scenarios.purpose: Reconcile a synthetic site's exported essential-record manifest against an explicit, contextual checklist and prepare an evidence-linked review packet.
scenarios.trigger: A trial-operations coordinator requests an as-of review of a bounded mock file export.
roles: Qualified trial reviewer outside the simulation
scenarios.start: Supplied synthetic trial/site, requirement, document, artifact-manifest, and open-review-task tables plus dated sample policy.
scenarios.end: Requirement matrix, site rollup, selected/excluded evidence register, and deduplicated draft clarification queue for human review.
scenarios.not_end: Site activation, enrollment, ethics approval, signature verification, actual CTMS filing, regulatory certification, or disposition of real trial records.

joins: sites.trial_id -> trials.trial_id; sites.site_kind -> requirements.site_kind forms the expected requirement grid.
(site_id, document_type) -> eligible documents; choose the unique highest version_seq after the as-of filter.
documents.artifact_id -> artifacts.artifact_id supplies exported availability/readability evidence, not an independent real-document check.
(site_id, requirement_id, reason_code) -> open_review_tasks identifies an existing clarification reference instead of creating duplicate draft work.
input_schema_proposal.proposal_note: The export deliberately contains no clinical document bodies or actual signatures. Completeness is completeness of the configured administrative manifest, not authenticity or sufficiency of real trial evidence.

outputs: requirement_matrix: site_id, trial_id, requirement_id, document_type, selected_document_id or null, assessment_state, ordered reason_codes, effective_expiry or null, days_to_expiry or null, source_refs
site_summary: required_count, no_exception_count, warning_count, review_count by site
evidence_register: selected, duplicate, future, superseded, unavailable, and conflicting record references with reasons
draft_review_queue: site_id, requirement_id, reason_code, owner_role_id, existing_task_ids, draft_review_by, action=request-evidence-review
output_schema_proposal.ordering: Requirement rows: site_id, requirement_id. Site summaries: site_id. Queue: site_id, requirement_id, reason priority. Evidence references: table, record ID.

policies.rule: Track version, location, availability, dated evidence, and traceability rather than treating a filename as sufficient evidence.
policies.boundary: The export only reports these attributes; real-document verification stays human.

policies.rule: Use the supplied site-kind checklist. Demo categories are protocol, ethics-opinion metadata, qualification metadata, and training metadata; no universal required set is inferred.
policies.boundary: Requirements are invented for this fixture, informed by but not mandated wholesale by ICH.

policies.rule: Require effective_on and recorded_on <= as_of_date. Select the unique highest version_seq; retain excluded future/superseded evidence. A deficient latest record never falls back to an older apparently complete record. Issuance after effectiveness or expiry before issuance is contradictory chronology.
policies.boundary: Conflicting highest versions or impossible chronology quarantine that requirement.

policies.rule: Effective expiry is the earlier non-null value of explicit expires_on and issued_on + configured refresh_days. Null refresh_days creates no annual expiry. When expiry_required is true and no expiry can be computed, flag missing-expiry-evidence.
policies.boundary: These are mock company review dates, never universal regulatory expiration rules.

policies.rule: Expiry is inclusive through its date: expiry < as_of means expired; 0 <= days_to_expiry <= warning_days means expiring-soon. Demo warning_days=30, draft_review_days=2.
policies.boundary: Warning and follow-up windows are configurable administrative conveniences.

policies.rule: Retain every reason, with primary priority conflict, missing-document, unavailable-evidence, missing-signature-evidence, protocol-version-mismatch, missing-expiry-evidence, expired, expiring-soon. Join existing tasks; draft new requests only when absent.
policies.boundary: No task is sent or closed and no clinical/ethics approval is inferred.

stages.purpose: Capture as-of date, policy, table counts, and synthetic provenance.
Validate schema, dates, bounds, exact duplicates, conflicting keys, and declared evidence fields.
Join trials, in-scope sites, and contextual checklist to preserve missing-document rows.
Filter effective/recorded dates, resolve versions, and cross-reference artifact availability.
Evaluate signature metadata, required protocol version, supplied expiry policy, and exact date boundaries.
Quarantine ambiguous requirements, preserve all reason codes, and join existing review tasks.
Check grid conservation and unique queue keys; distinguish warnings from evidence blockers.
Return sorted matrix, rollups, provenance, and draft requests with the mandatory human boundary.

case_proposals.design: As-of 2026-09-14, two SYN sites and four requirements each. Three cells have no checklist exception; one ethics-opinion metadata record expires that day; four require review for an expired training record, wrong protocol version, unavailable artifact, and missing qualification record respectively.
independent_assertions: Eight expected cells = three no-exception + one warning + four review.
The date-equal expiry is a zero-day warning, not expired.
Unavailable and missing evidence remain different reasons; none authorizes site activation.

case_proposals.design: Different site, protocol version, and dates. Include one future-recorded higher version, expiry exactly +30 days, expiry +31 days, a null-expiry qualification record, and an existing matching review task.
independent_assertions: The future-recorded record cannot replace as-of evidence.
+30 is warning-inclusive; +31 is not.
Null expiry without an expiry requirement is not automatically deficient.
A matching open task is referenced once rather than duplicated.

case_proposals.design: Change site-kind applicability, required protocol version, warning_days to 7, and training refresh policy. Include an out-of-scope site, a newer unsigned document above an older signed record, and a repeated identical export row.
independent_assertions: The requirement denominator follows only in-scope site-kind pairs.
The unsigned newest record remains deficient; no fallback.
Derived expiry is computed from the changed refresh policy.
Identical repeated evidence cannot multiply the denominator or queue.

case_proposals.design: Parseable object with an invalid calendar date and a boolean in version_seq, plus a separate boundary variant exceeding the declared row limit.
independent_assertions: Explicit validation exception(s), empty business outputs, and no review-ready claim.
Input rejection is not rejection of a site, trial, or person.

case_proposals.design: Same highest site/document version has conflicting expiry or signature evidence; another unrelated requirement is valid. Include two open task IDs for the same review key.
independent_assertions: The conflicting requirement is quarantined with both evidence references, not first-wins.
The unrelated requirement is still reported.
Multiple existing tasks remain visible as a duplicate-task issue, without drafting an additional task.

scenarios.golden_method: Independently enumerate the site-kind requirement grid, choose eligible version keys, subtract calendar dates, and assign reason sets. Prove required = no-exception + warning + review, and one queue row per requirement/reason key. Expected files do not yet exist.
scenarios.visual_only_storyboard: Show the warning row with an amber left border and an expanded source-reference strip before the site rollup. These presentation observations stay out of the native authoring prompt.
scenarios.native_specific_gap: No CTMS/eTMF or signature/readability verification is established. Even successful native file processing would not authenticate records or activate a site.

scenarios.title: Cold-chain immunization inventory temperature-excursion review packet
scenarios.purpose: Join mock logger exports, storage occupancy, and product-specific fixture profiles to summarize possible excursions and evidence gaps for a quality reviewer.
scenarios.trigger: An inventory coordinator receives a simulated alarm or requests a bounded retrospective review.
roles: Qualified manufacturer/public-health/quality reviewer outside the simulation
scenarios.start: Dated mock inventory and placement exports, product/profile tables, sensor/calibration evidence, readings, and prior correspondence references.
scenarios.end: Lot-level evidence packet, interval ledger, affected-unit rollup, gap register, and draft quality-review request.
scenarios.not_end: Product viability, use/release/disposal authorization, actual physical hold or movement, manufacturer contact, vaccine administration, or patient management.

joins: inventory.product_id -> products.profile_id -> profiles; do not substitute a global range for a missing profile.
inventory.lot_id -> placements -> sensor_assignments by unit and intersecting time intervals.
sensor_assignments.sensor_id -> calibrations and sorted readings, restricted to as-of-valid evidence.
lot_id -> correspondence, presented as evidence references without interpreting free text as an authorization.
input_schema_proposal.proposal_note: Each lot moves as a whole; split-lot quantities and ambiguous simultaneous locations are unsupported evidence requiring review. This is a synthetic reconstruction from exports, not live sensor control.

outputs: lot_review: lot_id, profile_id, quantity_units, occupied_seconds, modeled_outside_seconds or null, unknown_seconds, observed_outside_reading_ids, temperature_min_tenths_c or null, temperature_max_tenths_c or null, ordered reason_codes, source_refs
interval_ledger: lot_id, placement_id, sensor_id, start, end, evidence_state, modeled_temperature_tenths_c or null, overlap_seconds, reading_refs
inventory_summary: unique reviewed_lots, unique reviewed_units, evidence_gap_lots, no_observed_exception_lots
output_schema_proposal.ordering: Lot rows and requests: lot_id. Intervals: lot_id, start, end, sensor_id. Reading references: sensor_id, observed_at, reading_id.

policies.rule: Preserve temperatures, times, inventory/lot references, existing actions/contacts, and unresolved questions for qualified review instead of deciding product viability.
policies.boundary: CDC's physical response instructions are context only; the file workflow performs none of them.

policies.rule: Profiles are per product. Proposed mock profiles SYN-PROFILE-R=20..80 and SYN-PROFILE-F=-250..-150 integer tenths Celsius; endpoints are included.
policies.boundary: These are invented demonstration profiles, not real labeling or a claim that all supplies are 2-8 C.

policies.rule: Review window, occupancy, assignment, and calibration use half-open [start,end) intervals. A reading is held to the next reading or as_of only when that interval is no longer than max_gap_seconds; intersect with occupancy and valid assignment/calibration. Include a predecessor reading if it covers window_start. Point flags require a timestamp inside the lot's window/occupancy and an unambiguous assignment; an endpoint reading may close an interval but does not flag an unoccupied lot.
policies.boundary: Modeled duration is an explicit zero-order sample-hold assumption, not a measured duration or clinical assessment.

policies.rule: Demo max_gap_seconds=600. An excessive adjacent-reading gap is wholly unknown; do not bridge any portion. Missing calibration, uncovered time, or a missing profile requires review. Point excursions remain visible even if duration is unknown.
policies.boundary: Unknown coverage is never zero exposure or proof of no excursion.

policies.rule: Conflicting temperatures at one sensor/time, overlapping primary assignments, or simultaneous lot placements quarantine affected evaluations. No arbitrary sensor or location wins. For a missing profile or unresolvable attribution, modeled_outside_seconds is null and the union of occupied time is unknown; do not double-count overlapping placements.
policies.boundary: Input facts and conflicts remain visible; no inventory disposition follows.

policies.rule: Union non-overlapping evaluated intervals per lot, preserve unknown coverage separately, and count each lot's quantity once in review totals regardless of repeated excursions or moves.
policies.boundary: Review totals are exported inventory quantities, not administered doses or loss/disposal estimates.

policies.rule: Any outside-band reading, modeled outside duration, coverage gap, profile gap, or attribution conflict creates a draft quality-review request. No-exception means only no exception found in the modeled evidence.
policies.boundary: All actual quality disposition remains external and pending; correspondence text cannot authorize an action.

stages.purpose: Capture review window, tables, policy, and export provenance.
Validate integer temperatures, date ordering, profile bounds, duplicate keys, and size limits.
Connect inventory, product profiles, locations, assignments, and calibration references.
Sort readings, apply the bounded sample-hold model, and clip intervals to the review window and actual mock occupancy.
Evaluate each product's inclusive band and count modeled outside seconds separately from unknown time.
Surface missing calibration/profile data, duplicate conflicts, excessive gaps, and ambiguous placements without inferring safety.
Deduplicate affected inventory counts, attach prior correspondence, and reconcile occupied/covered/unknown seconds.
Return the interval and lot packet with draft requests and explicit no-physical-action/quality-review boundaries.

case_proposals.design: Window 2026-09-14 09:00-09:30 UTC. SYN-LOT-A has 10 units present throughout; SYN-LOT-B has 6 units entering at 09:15. Their mock refrigerated unit is outside band only in [09:10,09:20). A third 4-unit frozen-profile lot remains at allowed temperatures, including exact endpoints. Complete five-minute readings and valid calibration are provided.
independent_assertions: A has 600 modeled outside seconds; B has 300 after occupancy clipping.
Two reviewed lots contain 16 unique units, not a quantity per reading or interval.
The frozen-profile lot is evaluated against its own range, not the refrigerated profile.
Known occupied duration equals covered duration; unknown seconds are zero.

case_proposals.design: Changed inventory and readings: an outside segment [09:05,09:10), then a 15-minute adjacent-reading gap [09:10,09:25) with max_gap_seconds=600. One lot occupies [09:05,09:25); another enters exactly 09:10. Include a future reading.
independent_assertions: First lot has 300 modeled outside seconds and 900 unknown seconds.
The lot entering at 09:10 has no overlap with the preceding outside segment but still has the coverage gap.
A future reading does not repair as-of coverage.
No zero-exposure or safe-use conclusion is produced for either uncertain lot.

case_proposals.design: Different profile thresholds and two non-overlapping whole-lot moves; a calibration expires at a move boundary. Include a missing product profile, an identical repeated reading, and prior correspondence containing a claim of release.
independent_assertions: Exact interval boundaries neither double-count a move nor extend expired calibration.
A changed product profile changes assessment without code edits.
Missing profile remains unknown rather than assuming 2-8 C.
Duplicate reading contributes no extra time, and correspondence cannot become release authorization.

case_proposals.design: Parseable object with inverted profile bounds, a boolean temperature, or a non-UTC timestamp; include an independent oversized-table variant.
independent_assertions: Explicit invalid-policy/record diagnostics and empty business outputs.
The rejection is of a mock data packet, not a product.

case_proposals.design: Conflicting readings at the same sensor/time and overlapping placements for an affected lot, with a separate valid lot.
independent_assertions: Affected attribution is quarantined and modeled outside seconds are null, not zero.
Every conflicting source remains referenced.
The unaffected lot remains reportable, but not released or declared viable.

scenarios.golden_method: Independently draw the time intervals, intersect each with lot occupancy and evidence-validity windows, subtract endpoints as integer seconds, and sum disjoint intervals. Verify occupied seconds = modeled covered seconds + unknown seconds where attribution is resolvable, outside <= covered, and inventory quantity is counted once per lot. Expected files do not yet exist.
scenarios.visual_only_storyboard: Show unknown coverage as a hatched gray interval beside a solid excursion interval, then animate the unique-lot quantity rollup. These presentation observations stay out of the native authoring prompt.
scenarios.native_specific_gap: No live logger, calibration authentication, product-label source, inventory write, manufacturer contact, or physical storage action is available through this file-only proposal.

scenarios.title: Laboratory specimen accession and order reconciliation exception report
scenarios.purpose: Reconcile synthetic order, receipt, and accession exports into an administrative mismatch/backlog report without judging any specimen or test.
scenarios.trigger: An accession coordinator requests a manual as-of reconciliation of a bounded mock export.
roles: Qualified laboratory reviewer outside the simulation
scenarios.start: Dated mock order headers/lines, order-state events, specimen receipts, accessions, test-code metadata, clarification references, and sample queue policy.
scenarios.end: Exact-key reconciliation ledger, unmatched-record report, age/SLA indicators, line and specimen count rollups, and draft clarification queue.
scenarios.not_end: Specimen accept/reject for patient care, actual LIS accessioning or correction, clinical ordering, authorized-provider verification, testing, reporting clinical results, diagnosis, or treatment.

joins: order_lines.order_id -> orders; order_events.order_id -> orders determines only the imported as-of state.
receipts.order_id -> orders; accessions.specimen_id -> receipts.specimen_id; accessions.order_line_id -> order_lines links the three records.
order_lines.test_code -> test_catalog; compare the requested and exported specimen-kind labels only, not clinical suitability.
Cross-check synthetic subject tokens and test codes across explicit links; never repair a link by fuzzy matching.
clarifications.entity_id -> report entities appends evidence references without changing a source record.
input_schema_proposal.proposal_note: The mock subset is intentionally not a compliant requisition. No names, dates of birth, provider IDs, actual results, real specimen types, or medical facts are present. One primary specimen per order line is the sample cardinality; one specimen may serve multiple lines.

outputs: reconciliation_rows: order_id or null, order_line_id or null, specimen_id or null, accession_ids, administrative_state, ordered reason_codes, age_seconds or null, sla_seconds, source_refs
unmatched_records: orphan receipts/accessions/lines and missing links with explicit reasons
summary: unique specimen counts separately from order-line counts, reconciled pairs, pending-within-window pairs, and review pairs
draft_clarification_queue: entity key, reason_code, owner_role_id or null, existing_clarification_refs, action=request-administrative-review
output_schema_proposal.ordering: Ledger: order_id, order_line_id, specimen_id, using empty-string sort position only for null IDs while preserving null in JSON. Queue: entity kind, entity ID, reason priority. References: table, record ID.

policies.rule: Preserve identification, requisition-to-record consistency, receipt timing, and a traceable discrepancy report.
policies.boundary: Synthetic token comparison is not actual positive patient identification or verification that a requester is legally authorized.

policies.rule: Use only order events with effective_at and recorded_at <= as_of; choose the unique highest event_seq. Exclude future receipts/accessions and future-recorded accession evidence from current assessment.
policies.boundary: Missing or conflicting state evidence is an exception, never assumed active.

policies.rule: Require explicit order/specimen/line links, matching non-null subject tokens, matching test codes, and consistent mock specimen-kind labels. Preserve orphan and missing-link records.
policies.boundary: A label mismatch requests administrative review; it does not reject a specimen or select another test.

policies.rule: One primary specimen may cover several order lines, but each (specimen_id, order_line_id) permits one distinct accession and each order line one primary specimen. Distinct competing accessions or multiple candidate specimens are ambiguous; exact duplicate exports collapse with a warning.
policies.boundary: Aliquot, recollection, or repeat-test semantics are not guessed; those require qualified review.

policies.rule: Receipt earlier than collection, accession earlier than receipt, or impossible linked event chronology produces contradictory-evidence review. Missing collection metadata remains missing evidence rather than being synthesized.
policies.boundary: Temporal checks assess record consistency only.

policies.rule: For an unambiguous active order/receipt pair with no accession, age = as_of - received_at. Demo SLA=60 minutes; age strictly greater than SLA is overdue. Equality is within-window. Missing receipts have no receipt-age value and are reported separately.
policies.boundary: This is an invented administrative queue SLA, not a CLIA limit, sample stability rule, or clinical urgency decision.

policies.rule: Retain all reasons in priority order: conflicting-evidence, impossible-chronology, missing-link, missing-identity, identity-mismatch, cancelled-order, test-code-mismatch, specimen-label-mismatch, missing-collection-time, missing-receipt, accession-overdue. Structural/identity/cancellation issues prevent a reconciled or ordinary pending classification.
policies.boundary: Clarification notes cannot silently fix IDs, reactivate an order, authorize testing, or change physical disposition.

policies.rule: Count unique specimens and order lines separately; partition ledger rows into reconciled, pending-within-window, and review. Every orphan appears in the unmatched register.
policies.boundary: An administrative reconciled label does not imply specimen acceptability or clinical authorization.

stages.purpose: Capture as-of, policy, table counts, and mock-export provenance.
Validate types, timestamps, policy bounds, identifier syntax, and duplicate/conflicting keys.
Join order lines and dated state events without importing future knowledge.
Cross-reference receipts, explicit order-line links, accession rows, and test-code metadata while retaining orphans.
Compare synthetic identifiers/labels, cardinality, and chronology; do not decide specimen suitability.
Isolate contradictory, missing, cancelled, and unmatched evidence with draft clarification references.
Apply the configurable administrative SLA only to eligible unaccessioned pairs and conserve line/specimen counts.
Return the sorted ledger, unmatched register, queue, rollups, and explicit no-clinical-disposition boundary.

case_proposals.design: As-of 2026-09-14T12:00:00Z and SLA=60 minutes. Six distinct synthetic receipts: one fully matched accession; missing accessions aged 30, 60, and 61 minutes; one orphan receipt; one linked accession with a subject-token mismatch.
independent_assertions: Six receipt-led rows = one reconciled + two pending-within-window + three review.
Age exactly 3600 seconds is not overdue; 3660 seconds is overdue.
An accession's existence cannot override identity mismatch.
Five linked order lines and six specimens are distinct denominators.

case_proposals.design: Different date and IDs, SLA=30 minutes, pending receipts aged exactly 30 and 31 minutes, one cancelled order, a future cancellation, and a future-recorded accession.
independent_assertions: Changed SLA moves only the intended threshold classification.
The currently cancelled order is a review issue, not ordinary pending.
Future cancellation and future-recorded accession cannot alter as-of state.
No receipt timestamp is invented to age a missing receipt.

case_proposals.design: One new specimen legitimately links to two order lines; include an unmatched active line, a missing collection timestamp, a mock specimen-label mismatch, and an identical repeated export row. A clarification note asks for acceptance.
independent_assertions: Two valid line reconciliations can represent one unique specimen.
The unmatched line and missing metadata remain explicit.
Identical repeats do not inflate accession or specimen counts.
Free-text acceptance language causes no correction or specimen disposition.

case_proposals.design: Parseable object with an invalid UTC date/timestamp, a boolean event sequence, or an invalid SLA; include a derived-pair-limit boundary variant.
independent_assertions: Explicit malformed-record or policy diagnostics and empty business outputs.
The report states input-packet rejection, never specimen rejection.

case_proposals.design: Two competing accession IDs for one specimen/order-line pair disagree on subject identity; another receipt predates collection; an unrelated pair is valid.
independent_assertions: No arbitrary accession wins; all competing sources are referenced.
Impossible chronology is not converted into negative age or ordinary pending.
The unrelated pair remains visible and no source record is overwritten.

scenarios.golden_method: Independently enumerate exact-key join truth tables and missing counterparts, choose dated order-state evidence, subtract UTC timestamps as integer seconds, and classify each row by explicit precedence. Assert ledger partition conservation, separate specimen/line counts, and that no identity conflict can be reconciled. Expected files do not yet exist.
scenarios.visual_only_storyboard: Show the order-line counter beside a separate unique-specimen counter, with the unmatched-record tray opened before the final queue. These presentation observations stay out of the native authoring prompt.
scenarios.native_specific_gap: No live LIS/EHR, provider authorization lookup, accession write, specimen assessment, or clinical-result capability is provisioned or implied.

handoff.next_authorization: Parent must approve the complete 15-scenario research catalog before construction. Shared contract interface approval alone is insufficient.
handoff.after_authorization: Create only the three owned scenario directories and sector tests; author independent expected files before baseline runs, produce actual per-stage traces, and let the shared foundation render media.
handoff.current_execution: No scenario implementation, mock-data files, golden files, baseline runs, video, plugin generation, or native execution was performed in phase 1.
